name: Yu Pan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Confinity/PayPal around 1998–1999 as one of the original six founding members and built early payments and auction infrastructure while still in his early twenties (IMSA class of 1995; UIUC CS).
early_history_summary: Born in China and later educated in Illinois at the selective Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (class of 1995), then studied computer science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Max Levchin recruited him and fellow Illinois alum Russel Simmons into Confinity; he designed and implemented PayPal’s first flagship product and web technologies for eBay auction payments.
family_context_summary: Born in China; parents were concerned enough about startup risk that Levchin traveled to Illinois to reassure them. Broader family financial or professional background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IMSA, UIUC PayPal mafia, Max Levchin recruitment, Confinity founding team
evidence_summary: Yu Pan’s path ran through IMSA (class of 1995) and UIUC CS, then into the Confinity/PayPal founding team recruited by Max Levchin. Exact public birth date is missing, but IMSA 1995 graduation implies birth in the mid-to-late 1970s, so co-founding PayPal around 1998–1999 occurred well before age 26. He later became YouTube’s first employee, working on the early video player, then held roles at Google, Affirm, 8i (CTO), and Origin Protocol. Family domain advantage is not documented; primary leverage was elite peer cofounders and the payments/internet structural wave.
starting_point: Born in China; later attended IMSA and UIUC in Illinois; parental occupation and class background not documented beyond parental caution about startup risk.
current_position: R&D engineer at Origin Protocol; previously PayPal co-founder, YouTube first employee, Affirm engineer, and CTO of 8i.

trajectory.event: Graduated from the Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA class of 1995).
Joined as co-founder/founding engineer of Confinity/PayPal and built early payments and auction infrastructure.
Joined YouTube as its first employee and built the site’s early video player and distribution tech.
Joined Google following Google’s acquisition of YouTube.
Joined Origin Protocol as research and development engineer focused on decentralized marketplace tech.

name: Edmund Berkeley
milestone_by_age_26: No material computing milestone by age 26 found. Harvard BA in Mathematics and Logic in 1930 (age 21) and actuarial work at Prudential from 1934 are pre-computing career steps; ACM co-founding (1947) and Giant Brains (1949) came at ages 38–40.
early_history_summary: Attended St. Bernard's School and Phillips Exeter Academy, earned a Harvard BA in 1930, and worked as a Prudential Insurance actuary from 1934 with a WWII Navy interruption. His defining computing contributions—ACM co-founding, Giant Brains, and Simon—occurred in the late 1940s.
evidence_summary: Berkeley’s elite secondary schooling and Harvard degree placed him on a strong professional path, but his material computing milestones—co-founding ACM in 1947 and publishing Giant Brains in 1949—occurred well after age 26. No independently verifiable dated computing achievement by 26 was found.

name: Alissa Jay Abdullah
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Birth year not documented; public career highlights (White House Deputy CIO 2012–2015, Xerox CISO, Mastercard Deputy CSO) are mid/late-career executive roles, not dated early breakout achievements.
early_history_summary: Earned a BS in Mathematics at Savannah State University, an MS in telecommunications/computer networks from George Washington University, and a PhD in IT management from Capella. Began as a DoD cryptologic mathematician and later held senior security and CIO roles in industry and government.
evidence_summary: Abdullah is a notable cybersecurity executive (White House Deputy CIO, Mastercard Deputy CSO), but no public birth year or dated material achievement by age 26 was identified in reviewed sources.

name: Perry Alexander
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Completed BS/MS/PhD sequence at the University of Kansas spanning roughly 1980–1992; faculty distinction and I2S directorship came later. Birth year not published; no dated breakout achievement by 26 documented.
early_history_summary: Earned BSEE, BSCS, MSEE, and PhD in computer science/electrical engineering at the University of Kansas (studies spanning 1980–1992). Later joined KU faculty (1999), becoming AT&T Foundation Distinguished Professor and Director of the Institute for Information Sciences.
evidence_summary: Alexander is a distinguished KU formal-methods professor and research-institute director. A long multi-degree path ending in a 1992 PhD and later faculty leadership does not yield a clear, dated material milestone by age 26.

name: Tom Preston-Werner
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Gravatar in 2004 at age 25, creating a globally recognized avatar service later acquired by Automattic in 2007.
early_history_summary: Born May 27, 1979, in Dubuque, Iowa; father died in childhood, mother was a teacher and stepfather an engineer. Attended Dubuque Senior High School and spent two years at Harvey Mudd College before dropping out to build software products, founding Gravatar in 2004 and later co-founding GitHub in 2008.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Dubuque, Iowa; father died when he was a child; mother was a teacher and stepfather was an engineer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Stepfather was an engineer, providing some technical-household exposure; not a documented high-status industry pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ruby/open-source community, Gravatar, Harvey Mudd start, SF Ruby meetups, GitHub cofounders
evidence_summary: Preston-Werner built Gravatar at 25 and sold it to Automattic at 28, then co-founded GitHub in 2008 with Wanstrath, Hyett, and Chacon. Early advantage came less from family capital than from open-source/Ruby community distribution, product taste, and complementary cofounders. Family adversity (father’s death) and modest Midwest origin contrast with later Bay Area immersion. Microsoft’s GitHub acquisition made him a billionaire; he later co-founded Chatterbug and Preston-Werner Ventures and joined the Giving Pledge.
starting_point: Born in Dubuque, Iowa; father died in childhood; mother a teacher and stepfather an engineer.
current_position: Billionaire entrepreneur and investor (Preston-Werner Ventures); GitHub co-founder and former CEO; Giving Pledge participant; lives in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Founded Gravatar, a globally unique avatar service for blogs and web comments.
Co-founded GitHub and left a Microsoft/Powerset path to go full-time on the product.
Resigned as GitHub CEO after an internal investigation into workplace conduct.
Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5B, making Preston-Werner a billionaire from his stake.
With wife Theresa, committed to the Giving Pledge to donate the majority of their wealth.

name: Babak Nivi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Co-founded Venture Hacks (~2007) and AngelList (2010) with Naval Ravikant; MIT EECS credentials cluster around the late 1990s, implying AngelList founding well after age 26. Exact birth year not publicly established.
early_history_summary: MIT-trained (SB/MEng EECS; PhD candidate period around 1997 per secondary profiles). Partnered with Naval Ravikant on the Venture Hacks blog and launched AngelList in 2010 as a platform connecting startups and angels.
evidence_summary: Nivi’s defining public achievement is co-founding AngelList in 2010 after Venture Hacks. Without a verified birth year, and with education dated to the late 1990s, the AngelList milestone is not demonstrated to have occurred by age 26.

name: Kate Losse
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 confirmed. Joined Facebook in 2005 as employee #51 and later became Zuckerberg’s ghostwriter, but public birth year is missing so age at hire cannot be verified; fame largely arrived with The Boy Kings memoir (2012).
early_history_summary: Johns Hopkins–linked resume; described joining Facebook as a ‘grad school refugee’ in 2005 for customer support, later moving into internationalization and executive speechwriting before leaving around 2010 and publishing a critical memoir.
evidence_summary: Losse’s early Facebook employment is notable, but without a documented birth year the age-26 bar cannot be confirmed. Her major public recognition came with the 2012 memoir The Boy Kings.

name: Julian Bigelow
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Enrolled at MIT at 17 and earned a master’s in electrical engineering around 1935–1936 (age ~22–23), but defining work—Wiener fire-control collaboration, 1943 cybernetics paper, and IAS machine chief engineer from 1946—came at ages ~30–33.
early_history_summary: Born March 19, 1913 in Nutley, New Jersey; MIT EE/math master’s in the mid-1930s; early industry work (e.g., Sperry) preceded WWII collaboration with Norbert Wiener and the 1946 IAS Electronic Computer Project under von Neumann.
family_context_summary: Fourth of five siblings; born in Nutley, New Jersey. Broader family financial/professional status not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Bigelow became a pioneering computer engineer as chief engineer of the IAS machine, but that work began in 1946 at age 33. An MIT master’s at ~22–23 is strong training, not a material public breakthrough under this rubric.

name: Daphne Koller
milestone_by_age_26: Earned a bachelor’s degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1985 at age 17, followed by a master’s at 18 (1986) and a Stanford PhD in computer science in 1993 at age 24–25.
early_history_summary: Born August 27, 1968 in Jerusalem; father a botanist and mother an English teacher. Attended college in parallel with high school, finished an MSc in CS at 18, completed Israeli military service, then earned a Stanford PhD under Joseph Halpern (1993) before a Berkeley postdoc with Stuart Russell and joining Stanford faculty in 1995.
family_context_summary: Born in Jerusalem, Israel; father was a botanist and mother an English teacher. Family supported unconventional acceleration (college in parallel with high school).
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were academics/educators (botany and English teaching), providing a high-education household; not a direct computer-science family firm, but strong academic culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: BSc at 17, MSc at 18, Stanford PhD at 25, Hebrew University, Halpern advisee, MacArthur Fellow
evidence_summary: Koller’s path is a clear intellectual-prodigy trajectory: BSc at 17, MSc at 18, Stanford PhD by ~25, then Berkeley postdoc and Stanford faculty by 27. She became a leading figure in probabilistic graphical models, a MacArthur Fellow (2004), co-founded Coursera with Andrew Ng (2012), later led computing at Calico, and founded ML-driven drug-discovery company insitro (2018). Academic parents and elite institutions accelerated a pre-existing cognitive edge rather than substituting for it.
starting_point: Born in Jerusalem, Israel, to a botanist father and English-teacher mother; accelerated through university while still of high-school age.
current_position: Founder and CEO of insitro, a machine-learning drug discovery company; former Coursera co-founder/president and Stanford CS professor; NAS member.

trajectory.event: Received bachelor’s degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem at age 17.
Completed master’s degree in computer science at Hebrew University at age 18.
Earned PhD in computer science at Stanford under Joseph Halpern.
Joined the Stanford University computer science faculty.
Named a MacArthur Foundation Fellow for work in AI and probabilistic models.
Co-founded Coursera with Andrew Ng and helped popularize large-scale MOOCs.
Founded insitro to apply machine learning to drug discovery after leaving Calico.

name: Alexis Battle
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 confirmed. Stanford BS in 2003, multi-year industry interval (including Google), then MS/PhD in computer science in 2013; defining faculty leadership at Johns Hopkins came after the PhD. Birth year not published.
early_history_summary: Stanford BS (2003) then MS and PhD in computer science (2013); worked in industry including Google between degrees. Joined Johns Hopkins faculty and became Wu and Zhang Professor across Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and Genetic Medicine.
evidence_summary: Battle is a leading computational genomics researcher at JHU, but the dated public milestones (BS 2003, PhD 2013, faculty career thereafter) do not establish a material breakout by age 26 without a verified birth year and early flagship achievement.
